steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Coat a 9x4-inch loaf pan with cooking spray.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl; set aside.

Beat together sugar and butter with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth. Add mashed bananas and mix until combined. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in milk and vanilla.
Stir in flour mixture, walnuts, and chocolate chips until just incorporated. Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan. Tap pan on the counter to release any air pockets.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 1 hour and 10 minutes. Let rest in the pan for 15 to 20 minutes. Remove bread from the pan, then slice and serve.

review.reviewBody: I increased the vanilla to a full teaspoon, used pecans instead of walnuts and mini chocolate chips. I made muffins out of this recipe--I actually got 12 really big muffins out of one recipe. I baked them at 350* for 22 minutes. I did let them cool in the pan overnight. I make A LOT of banana bread and A LOT of muffins (my family can eat 12 muffins in one day and that's on a slow day) and I think this is one of the best banana breads I've ever made. My husband called to tell me from work that HE thinks this is one of the better banana bread recipes I've made......and that's huge coming from him. This one's a keeper.

I make this all the time, now! My kids love it. I usually double it and freeze a loaf. I leave out the nuts. I have a hard time getting quick breads to bake evenly so I use the convection setting on my oven and lower it by 25 degrees. You really have to watch it because if you bake too long the bottom gets tough.

I usually make the recipe from this site Banana Banana Bread, but I love Chef John and I thought I would give this a try. Hands down, best banana bread (or muffins which I made in this case) EVER! I will only use this recipe from now on! The muffins (which made 24 and took 18 minutes in my Kitchenaid oven) were light, fluffy, and scrumptious! The addition in this recipe of baking powder, vanilla, and additional salt makes all the difference. I did omit the chocolate, but I'm sure they would be even more delicious with it. As always, thank you Chef John!

Awesome recipe!! Super easy to make, too. However, it only took me ~50 minutes to cook, due to the fact that I have a convection oven. I also didn't do the two mixtures in separate bowls, left out the walnuts, and added about 2-4x as many chocolate chips as it called for, but it's still perfect! 10/10, would recommend!!

Very good indeed. But I suspect maybe another banana (4 instead of 3) might somehow add more moisture and flavor to this already yummy recipe… Knowing I always mess up even with simple recipe, I stuck to the original (recipe) just in case it doesn’t come together. Reading other posts, I wish I had added a bit more vanilla extract and banana. Overall, it’s a wonderful recipe that’s a keeper. My go-to when baking banana bread, is always using the mini-loaf pan instead of the bigger loaf pan so I can share them with friends and not feel guilty eating all these.

I've made a lot of banana bread over the years and have been making this one the last few times. It is definitely the very best!! I make it a smidge fancier by slicing a banana lengthwise and arranging the slices on top. Then I top those bananas with a little honey, dark brown sugar and flaky sea salt. I learned this from Joshua Weissman on YouTube. I used his recipe for sourdough banana bread but this sweet recipe is my favorite of all! Oh, I also go extra and toast the walnuts first.

I haven't made banana bread in a long time. I am so happy I came across this recipe. I did read some of the reviews and decided to make muffins instead. I got 14 jumbo muffins. I used 4 bananas, instead of 3, dark chocolate chips instead of semi-sweet, and also used 1tsp of vanilla. I baked in 350° oven for about 24 mins, until toothpick came out clean. They are delicious! I will definitely be making these again!

I reduced the sugar from 1 cup to 1/3 cup, and it was plenty sweet enough. I find most banana bread recipes have way too much sugar. Next time I might take it down to 1/4 cup. I also used 1 cup whole wheat flour and 1 cup white flour instead of 2 cups white flour, and threw in about 1/3 cup ground flax seeds. Last, I substituted small chunks of tamarind instead of chocolate chips - that gives a tangier flavor than raisins but it's my husband's favorite.

This is the best banana bread that I've ever tried. The texture is perfect, moist but not dense. I did modify the recipe slightly for my taste. I increased the vanilla to 1 teaspoon, added 1 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg and 1/8 teaspoon of cloves which gave it a bit of spice without being a predominant flavor. Delicious!

Great banana bread recipe! I’m vegan and my son has an egg allergy, so I subbed aquafaba for the eggs (3tbs for each egg - 6tbs total) and added just a sprinkle of cinnamon and nutmeg. It came out PERFECT. Not dense, great flavor, moist with a perfect crust. I’ll be making this again and again.

Came out great! My 13 yr old couldn’t stay away. Only ingredients I added were 1 tbs of cinnamon and 1/4 c of brown sugar. I left out the chocolate chip just added walnuts and pecans. Will keep this recipe for many years to come.
I tripled this recipe and made 2 big loaves & 8 mini loaves. Absolutely delicious!
I use milk chocolate instead of dark and half the amount

I followed the recipe as written and made muffins. Since I only had a 6 count large muffin tin, I made 6 large and 5 cupcake size muffins. The large were baked for 30 min and the cupcake for 20 min. They both came out moist and fluffy. I'll definitely make this again!
Ever since my Mom sent me this recipe, I bake this 1-2x a month for my husband and I. My husband loves this recipe and I cant wait to bring it to family events this holiday season!

I'll never ever ever understand how people rate a recipe, then proceed to tell you all of the changes they made to it. You didn't use THIS recipe then...you changed this recipe...So...what are you rating?! God it drives me insane. All that aside, I actually used this exact recipe and it is good, but I think a teaspoon of salt was a bit too much. It's just ever so slightly too salty for me. (I used unsalted butter so I know that didn't add to it). So next time, I'm going to add half a teaspoon of salt and see how that turns out. Otherwise, I think the recipe is excellent.

They turned out great! Since I made individual portions, they cooked much quicker. 30 minutes bake time, so definitely keep an eye on them as different oven cook differently. Moist, flavorful, and perfect for grab-and-go servings.

It was fantastic! In my oven it took about 55 minutes to bake,but I don't know if that's because I added bout 1/2 cup flour to mine. I also added some spices like nutmeg and cinnamon but the basic recipe was really a good one.

Chef John, you better check the volume of butter! Why does your video appear to use half a stick of butter (1/4 cup) while the actual recipe calls for 1/2 cup of butter. I followed the recipe and my batter looked thinner than yours in the video and the end product was much "wetter". Signed, Confused

1. You don’t need old bananas. Brown your yellow bananas by placing them on a baking sheet in the oven on 300 degrees for 15-20 minutes. Allow to cool and cut them off and squeeze the softened bananas into a bowl including the natural juices. This will turn your mashing time in to less than 30 seconds. 2. Use 4 bananas 3. I used a bundlette pan and cooked for 20-25 minutes. 4. I made a glaze: 1 tsp Pancake Syrup, 4 tsp of butter, 1 cup of confectioners sugar, a sprinkle of salt and heavy cream as needed for binding and consistency. After it sets I microwaved some butter and went over the glaze again. It gives it like a salty sweet crunch.
